mechanism: Train 500 weak ELM (single-hidden-layer) classifiers in parallel on bootstrap samples of OHLC-derived digital-filter features; prune to odd best-by-mean(F1) members; combine continuous supports by averaging or majority vote into a binary direction label.
data_needed: OHLCV quotes; PrepareData digital filters (v.fatl,v.rbci,v.ftlm,...); outlier capping + normalization; HINoV.Mod ranked predictors; ZigZag/Class target 0/1; bootstrap holdout ratio r.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Terminal Cotir quotes (FX-style OHLCV); bar-indexed splits pretrain4000/train1000/val500/test250; depth retention tested to ~750 bars.
why_new_for_mis: Gives MIS a fast, diversity-driven neural ensemble sensor for directional regime that stays calibrated longer out-of-sample than a single DNN.
quote: After training, the ensemble retains its classification quality to a depth of more than half the size of the training set. In this case, the quality is retained for up to 750 bars, which is significantly higher than the same figure obtained on DNN (250 bars).

mechanism: Compute a robust D1 ATR by first averaging High–Low over ~7 days, then re-averaging only bars within [0.3,1.5]× that pre-ATR (discard spikes and tiny bars); fall back to plain ATR5 if fewer than 2 medium bars—used as percent-of-ATR Stop Loss sizing input.
data_needed: CopyRates D1 High/Low for last 7 days; pre_atr mean; filtered atr/count.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Stock names (TripAdvisor, Sberbank, ...), YM, Brent; strategy tested on M15 with D1 ATR; also percent-of-price SL variant.
why_new_for_mis: Gives MIS a spike-robust daily range/volatility sensor (Gerchik-style) rather than raw ATR polluted by outliers.
quote: the bars having the size over 1.5 7-day ATR and bars less than 0.3 of 7-day ATR are discarded

mechanism: Use pruned (or all 500) continuous ELM ensemble outputs as meta-features; train a Keras/TF dense net (softmax DNN(7,2) or deeper DNN500 with BN/dropout/GaussianNoise) as a trainable stacking combiner instead of fixed averaging/voting.
data_needed: ELM InputTrain/InputTest/InputTest1 matrices; binary Class from ZigZag sign; optional early-stopping on val_acc.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Same FX Cotir pipeline as Parts VI–VII; two feature families X1 (filters) and X2 (OHLC diffs CO/HO/LO/HL/dC/dH/dL).
why_new_for_mis: Turns base-learner support scores into a second-stage neural sensor that can learn non-linear combination and reduce squared bias vs plain averaging.
quote: Replacing the averaging of the ensemble outputs with the softmax function of a simple neural network reduces the bias by an order of magnitude without any noticeable decrease in the variance.

mechanism: Fit varbvs logistic Bayesian variable selection over all 500 ELM outputs to pick a sparse subset of base voters (e.g. X18,X5,X255 with pip≈1) and use that sparse model as an alternative combiner sensor.
data_needed: 500-dimensional InputTrain continuous predictions; binomial y; logodds grid.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Same splits as stacking experiments; Acc≈0.78 on InputTest in reported run.
why_new_for_mis: Offers a sparse Bayesian meta-sensor that selects which ensemble members are currently informative—useful as an adaptive confidence/ensemble-health channel for MIS.
quote: The logistic regression model obtained with the help of Bayesian variable selection (varbvs package) shows very good results.

mechanism: Before entry, require recent M1 and M15 High–Low amplitudes (per candle and channel span) below fixed point caps, plus adjacent-bar amplitude ratio in [1.1, 3.0], modeling a quiet horizontal channel with moderate end-of-channel activity.
data_needed: M1 and M15 OHLC of last 3 bars; Point-scaled amplitude thresholds (e.g. 200/300 points).
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD, USDCHF, USDJPY on M1 EA with M15/H1 context; demo Reduce_risks.
why_new_for_mis: Concrete multi-timeframe amplitude-channel sensor for 'entry-safe volatility' rather than a single ATR/StdDev reading.
quote: To reduce this risk, we can set the following condition in the entry algorithm: threshold amplitude limit in the nearest quote history.

mechanism: Exit any open position if Bid reverses from current M1 or M15 Open by ≥N points within a short wall-clock window (≤20s on M1, ≤120s on M15) or if the prior completed M1 candle body ≥200 points against the position—sensing sudden collapse/spike regime change.
data_needed: Live Bid; TimeCurrent; M1/M15 Open; prior M1 body.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: M1 primary with M15; examples GBPUSD Brexit collapse, USDCHF Oct 2015.
why_new_for_mis: Gives MIS a latency-aware crash/spike change sensor keyed to open-to-price velocity, not lagging MACD-style indicators.
quote: The limits of the price reverse deviation (collapse) are set relative to the current candle's Open level separately on different timeframes (in our case, these are М1 and М15).

mechanism: Stack candle direction, Fibo-period MA hierarchy (5>8>13), price-vs-MA location, body share >50%, wick/correction depth <25%, and High/Low progression across M1+M15 (+H1 MA24) to sense clear trend vs flat/unclear regime; ablation shows disabling activity block hurts net profit most.
data_needed: Multi-TF OHLC; SMA(5,8,13,60) on M1; SMA(4,8) on M15; SMA(24) on H1.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD/USDCHF/USDJPY; M1 entry with M15/H1 confirmation.
why_new_for_mis: Formalizes 'process activity' as the dominant regime filter—MIS can treat body%/MA-hierarchy confluence as a trend-clarity score.
quote: the most significant risk (at least for the given EA) is the one associated with the absence of a clearly defined trend (insufficient process activity).

mechanism: Sense entry when unified basket WPR difference (base−quote) crosses its MA with |Δ before| and |Δ after| in [2%,50%]; exit on opposite 'bad' (unclear) cross; H4 beats H1 on major FX pairs in tests.
data_needed: testWPReur/testWPRusd basket WPRs; MA of their difference; Delta1/Delta2 thresholds.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD, GBPUSD, AUDUSD, NZDUSD, USDCAD, USDCHF, USDJPY; H1 and H4 (D1 sparse).
why_new_for_mis: Cross-basket oscillator-vs-MA clarity filter is a pair-relative regime-change sensor, not a single-symbol MA cross.
quote: the distance between the unified indicator graph and the moving average before and after the breakthrough is not less than the one (Delta1 and Delta2) specified

mechanism: Display base and quote currency baskets separately; treat simultaneous opposite exhaustion (one basket overbought, other oversold) plus optional fast/slow MA cross and zero-line behavior as a stronger pair-regime/reversal cue than the combined line alone.
data_needed: Per-currency unified WPR (or STOCH/RSI) baskets; overbought/oversold levels ±50/±60; optional divergence check.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: NZDUSD, USDCAD examples on H1; method general to FX majors.
why_new_for_mis: Splits pair regime into two currency-state sensors whose confluence is the tradeable signal—natural MIS multi-asset regime feature.
quote: Simultaneous combination of such states of the baskets creates a picture... where the combined indicator graph for NZDUSD enters the overbought area with the subsequent breakthrough

mechanism: On pretrain only, run NoiseFiltersR::GE to find ~20% noisy labeled bars; train parallel ELM bagging ensembles on origin vs repaired vs removed vs 3-class-relabeled targets; repaired/removed consistently lift F1 vs origin.
data_needed: Labeled feature+Class pretrain frame; GE(k,kk) repaired indexes/labels; optional third class for noise.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Same digital-filter/ZigZag Class pipeline as Parts VI–VII; bar splits 4000/1000/500/250.
why_new_for_mis: Treats label noise as a first-class sensing/pretrain problem—MIS can maintain a 'ambiguous bar' class instead of forcing binary regime labels.
quote: processing the noise samples using the repaired and removed methods significantly improves the classification quality of ensembles

mechanism: Optimize ELM/postprocess thresholds (half/med/mce/both); build superensembles from top runs per denoise group; cascade majority votes into labels {-1,0,1} where 0=abstain; cascaded vote reached Balanced Acc≈0.836 on reported Test.
data_needed: Per-NN continuous scores; GetThreshold types; optimization Pred history; Ytest with 0→-1 remap.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Same FX feature/target setup; Acc lift 5–7% vs single-ensemble averaging.
why_new_for_mis: Adds an explicit abstain/uncertainty class from cascaded ensemble disagreement—directly usable as MIS confidence/regime-clarity output.
quote: If "-1", it is "Sell", "1" is "Buy", and "0" is "not sure".

mechanism: How-to for enabling private MQL5 Signals account monitoring dashboards; no market-state sensing method.
why_new_for_mis: Full read is platform UI/ops promo only—no regime/vol/liquidity/neural sensor.
quote: Trading account monitoring provides a detailed report on all completed deals.

mechanism: Marketplace headcount/rent/free-product promo; no sensing algorithm.
why_new_for_mis: No MIS sensing content—store marketing notice.
quote: The largest store of ready-made applications for algo-trading now features 13,970 products.

mechanism: Promo for embedding MetaQuotes Economic Calendar widget on websites; does not build a sensing pipeline in the article.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Macro calendar events (500 indicators); no traded instrument sensing.

quote: Almost a thousand web resources around the world feature the Economic Calendar widget.

mechanism: For each stock/ETF symbol, count D1 gaps and fraction where the day closes in the gap direction (confirmed); plot % across NASDAQ SnP100, MICEX20, ETFs, FTSE350, DAX100, CAC40—most cluster ~50%±6% with rare >65% continuation/reversal outliers.
data_needed: D1 OHLC per symbol group file; gap_total vs gap_confirmed; confirmed_per.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: US/UK/DE/FR/RU equities & ETFs; D1 only (ABBV example 758 bars from 2015).
why_new_for_mis: Cross-sectional overnight gap-follow-through sensor identifies which names have non-coin-flip gap regimes—MIS can score instruments by gap persistence.
quote: after a gap, the probabilities of a continued movement and a reversal are close to 50%... there are securities with the probabilities (of both continuation and reversal) considerably higher than 65%.

mechanism: Pull M1 closes via MetaTrader5 Python API for a watchlist; build return correlation heatmap; for highly correlated pairs (e.g. GBPUSD vs GBPJPY) run Engle–Granger cointegration and plot normalized spread z-score with ±2 bands as a relative-value sensor.
data_needed: MT5CopyRatesFromPos closes; pct_change corr matrix; statsmodels.coint; z=(diff-mean)/std.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD,GBPUSD,USDJPY,USDCHF,AUDUSD,GBPJPY on M1 (1000 bars); also EURUSD OHLC/Plotly and tick bid/ask viz.
why_new_for_mis: Packages live multi-pair correlation + cointegration z-score as an MIS cross-asset relationship sensor fed from MT5 ticks/bars.
quote: We can see a good correlation between GBPUSD and GBPJPY in the above heat map. Then we can test the co-integration
